examples.en: My older brother took over our father's family business.
Our family business has been farming for generations.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 삼대째 가업으로 이어지고 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has been passed down as a family business for three generations.
A family business is often passed on to one's children.
My father devoted his whole life to the family business.

examples.ko: 가업도 시대에 맞게 바뀌어야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think even a family business has to change with the times.

explain: 대대로 집안에서 이어 오는 일을 말하고, '가업을 잇다/물려받다/물려주다'처럼 써요. 그냥 '가게'와 달리 대를 이어 간다는 뜻이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: I will carry on my father's family business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.
phrases.en_equiv: to carry on the family business

phrases.en: My older brother inherited the family restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the receiver's side.

phrases.en: My grandfather passed the family business to his son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 사람 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the giver's side.
phrases.en_equiv: to hand down the family business

explain_en: It means the work a family carries on over generations, used as '가업을 잇다/물려받다/물려주다'. Unlike a plain '가게', it carries the idea of handing it down.

examples.en: The pool lifeguard blew a whistle.
Ask the parking lot attendant for directions.
My father works as a forest fire watcher.

examples.ko: 감시원은 하루 종일 한 자리에 서 있어요.
examples.en: The watchman stands in one spot all day.

examples.ko: 해수욕장에서 감시원 아저씨가 위험하다고 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: At the beach, the lifeguard told us it was dangerous.
A notice went up saying they are hiring more watchers.

explain: '경비원'은 건물이나 구역을 지키는 사람이고, '감시원'은 수영장, 산불처럼 무언가를 살피는 역할 앞에 장소나 일을 붙여 '수영장 감시원'처럼 써요. 사람을 의심한다는 느낌보다 안전을 살피는 일이라는 느낌으로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 산불 감시원이 산에서 연기가 나는지 살펴요.
phrases.en: The forest fire watcher checks whether there is smoke on the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 살필 대상을 붙여 어떤 감시원인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put what is being watched before the word to say what kind of watcher it is.

phrases.en: The pool monitor is keeping an eye on the children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 안전한지 살피는 일이라는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of someone watching to keep people safe.

phrases.en: I work as a watcher at a parking lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 맡은 일을 말할 때 '-(으)로 일하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -(으)로 일하다 to talk about a job or role.

explain_en: '경비원' is a guard who protects a building or area, while '감시원' is someone whose job is to watch over something, with the place or task in front, as in '수영장 감시원'. It usually sounds like safety monitoring rather than suspicion.

en: to have two jobs at the same time; to take up a sideline

examples.ko: 직장인이 부업을 겸업하는 경우가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More office workers are doing a side job alongside their main one.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 직원이 겸업하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: At our company, employees are not allowed to hold two jobs.
He works as both a writer and an instructor.

examples.ko: 은행이 보험 판매를 겸업할 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: Banks have become able to sell insurance as well.
Because I hold two jobs, I do not even have enough time to sleep.

examples.ko: 가게와 배달을 겸업한 뒤로 수입이 늘었어요.
examples.en: My income went up after I started running the shop and deliveries together.

explain: 본업 말고 덧붙이는 '부업'과 달리, 두 가지 일을 함께 하는 것에 초점이 있어요. 회사 규정이나 뉴스에서는 '겸업 금지', '겸업 허용'처럼 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 겸업 금지 규정이 있어요.
phrases.en: This company has a rule that bans holding a second job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 규정에서 가장 흔히 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in company rules.

phrases.en: These days some companies allow second jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 기관이 두 가지 일을 해도 된다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a company allows employees to work two jobs.

phrases.example: 그는 낮에는 회사원이고 밤에는 작가를 겸업하고 있어요.
phrases.en: He works as an office worker by day and also as a writer at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 두 가지 일을 함께 하고 있다는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current state of doing two jobs together.

explain_en: Unlike '부업', a side job added to your main work, the focus here is on doing two jobs together. In company rules and the news it often appears as '겸업 금지' (dual employment banned) or '겸업 허용' (allowed).

examples.en: My father runs a small restaurant.
I want to run a company myself.

examples.ko: 호텔을 경영한 지 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been ten years since I started running the hotel.
They say running a business is not easy.
I learned a lot while running the store.
How will you run the school from now on?

explain: 회사나 가게의 돈, 사람, 일을 책임지고 이끌 때 써요. 작은 가게는 '운영하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '경영하다'는 회사나 사업 같은 큰 곳에 어울려요.

phrases.en: My older brother runs a small shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 가게나 모임에는 '경영하다'보다 '운영하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For small shops or groups, '운영하다' sounds more natural.

phrases.en: My uncle has been running a business for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사업'과 함께 쓰면 큰 일을 책임진다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '사업' it suggests taking responsibility for a larger enterprise.

phrases.en: Managing a company is not easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 일'로 하는 일 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-는 일' talks about the activity itself.

explain_en: It means taking charge of the money, people and work of a company or shop. '운영하다' is used more for small shops, while '경영하다' fits companies and businesses.

dis.h: run a business as an owner or boss

examples.en: That person is a craftsperson who makes ceramics.

examples.ko: 공예가의 작업실에 가서 나무 그릇 만드는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I went to the craftsperson's studio and watched them make a wooden bowl.

examples.ko: 저는 어른이 되면 공예가가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: When I grow up, I want to become a craftsperson.
Famous craftspeople gathered and held an exhibition.
My friend ordered a small keychain from a craftsperson.
My uncle, who works as a craftsperson, is always busy.

explain: 도자기, 목공, 금속, 섬유처럼 손으로 쓸모 있고 아름다운 물건을 만드는 사람에게 써요. 그림을 그리는 '화가', 조각을 하는 '조각가'와 분야가 달라요. 직업을 말할 때는 '공예가', 만든 작품은 '공예품'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My uncle is a famous ceramic craftsman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분야 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어떤 공예를 하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the field in front to say what kind of craft they do.

phrases.en: I want to become a craftsman later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: I looked at the craftsman's works at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 만든 사람과 작품을 이어 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle '의' links the maker to the work.

explain_en: It is used for a person who makes useful and beautiful objects by hand, such as ceramics, woodwork, metalwork or textiles. It is a different field from '화가' (painter) and '조각가' (sculptor). The person is a '공예가' and the thing they make is a '공예품'.

examples.en: That engineering scientist researches robot arms.
My father works as an environmental engineering researcher.
Engineering researchers developed a new battery.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 꿈은 유명한 공학자가 되는 거였어요.
examples.en: As a child, my dream was to become a famous engineering scientist.

examples.ko: 공학자의 설명을 들으니 원리가 쉽게 이해됐어요.
examples.en: After hearing the engineering researcher's explanation, I understood the principle easily.

examples.ko: 이 다리는 여러 공학자의 노력으로 완성됐어요.
examples.en: This bridge was completed through the efforts of many engineering researchers.

explain: 공학자는 연구실에서 기술을 연구하는 사람에 가깝고, 현장에서 일하는 사람은 '엔지니어'나 '기술자'라고 해요. 앞에 '기계, 화학, 환경'을 붙여 분야를 말하는 경우가 많아요. 과학 이론을 연구하는 사람은 '과학자'예요.

phrases.en: An environmental engineering scientist checks whether the river water is clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 분야를 붙여서 어떤 연구를 하는지 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a field in front tells exactly what kind of research the person does.

phrases.example: 기계 공학자가 새 자동차 엔진을 만들었어요.
phrases.en: A mechanical engineering scientist built a new car engine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 연구하고 설계하는 분야의 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a person who researches and designs machines.

phrases.en: I want to become an engineering scientist later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 '되다'와 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 되다 when talking about dreams or careers.

explain_en: 공학자 leans toward someone who researches technology, while people working on site are called 엔지니어 or 기술자. A field is usually put in front, such as 기계, 화학 or 환경. Someone studying scientific theory is a 과학자.

examples.ko: 그는 우리 학교 발전에 크게 공헌했어요.
examples.en: He contributed greatly to our school's development.

examples.ko: 팀 승리에 공헌한 선수에게 상을 줬어요.
examples.en: They gave an award to the player who contributed to the team's win.

examples.ko: 지역 사회에 공헌하고 싶어서 봉사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to give back to the community, so I started volunteering.
An employee who served the company for a long time is retiring.

examples.ko: 제가 이 일에 얼마나 공헌했는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know how much I contributed to this work.
I want to be recognized in proportion to what I contribute.

explain: '도움이 되다'보다 무거운 표현이라서 오랫동안 크게 힘을 보탠 일에 써요. 가볍게 한 번 도운 일에는 어색해요. '기여하다'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 주로 '~에 공헌하다' 모양으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 지역 경제에 크게 공헌했어요.
phrases.en: That company contributed greatly to the local economy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '크게'를 붙이면 공헌의 크기를 분명히 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 크게 makes the size of the contribution clear.

phrases.en: We remember the people who contributed to the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공헌한' 뒤에 사람을 붙여 업적을 남긴 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a noun after 공헌한 to talk about someone who made a lasting contribution.

phrases.en: This research contributed to the advance of medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공헌하다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 공헌하다, and more common in writing and the news.

explain_en: It is heavier than 도움이 되다 and fits a large, long-term contribution. It sounds odd for a small one-time favor. It is nearly interchangeable with 기여하다 and usually appears as ~에 공헌하다.

p.n: 기여 is neutral and common; 공헌 stresses a merit that deserves praise.

examples.en: The teacher stepped onto the platform and explained.
Standing at the front of the class still makes me nervous.

examples.ko: 아버지는 삼십 년 동안 교단을 지키셨어요.
examples.en: My father stayed in the teaching profession for thirty years.

examples.ko: 저는 대학을 졸업하고 교단에 서고 싶어요.
examples.en: After graduating, I want to become a teacher.
Students gave presentations in front of the teacher's platform.

examples.ko: 그분은 올해 교단을 떠나 작가가 됐어요.
examples.en: This year she left teaching and became a writer.

explain: 교단은 교실 앞쪽에 선생님이 서는 조금 높은 자리예요. 비유로 '교단에 서다'라고 하면 교사로 일한다는 뜻이고, '교단을 떠나다'는 교사를 그만둔다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 이런 비유 표현으로 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 저는 이십 년 동안 교단에 섰어요.
phrases.en: to work as a teacher
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 단 위에 선다는 뜻이 아니라 교사로 일한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not about standing on the platform; it means working as a teacher.
phrases.en_equiv: to stand in front of the class

explain_en: 교단 is the slightly raised spot at the front of a classroom where the teacher stands. Figuratively, '교단에 서다' means working as a teacher and '교단을 떠나다' means leaving teaching. In daily life you hear it more in these figurative phrases.

examples.en: Many young people look for jobs after graduation.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 한국 회사에 구직하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm applying for jobs at Korean companies now.

examples.ko: 구직해 본 사람은 이력서 쓰기가 힘든 걸 알아요.
examples.en: People who have looked for a job know how hard it is to write a résumé.
Before job hunting, I prepared my cover letter first.

examples.ko: 구직할 때는 면접 연습을 꼭 하세요.
examples.en: When you look for a job, be sure to practice for interviews.

examples.ko: 구직했지만 아직 연락이 안 와서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I applied, but I haven't heard back yet, so I'm worried.

explain: 뉴스와 공공 서류에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '일자리를 찾고 있어요'나 '취업 준비 중이에요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '구직'과 짝은 일할 사람을 구하는 '구인'이에요.

phrases.en: These days I look for a job every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이력서를 내고 면접을 보는 일 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers the whole process of sending résumés, interviewing, and so on.
phrases.en_equiv: to carry out a job search

phrases.en: I'm looking for a job in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '구직하다'보다 훨씬 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in conversation than 'gujikhada.'

phrases.en: I'm preparing to get a job these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 얻으려고 공부하거나 준비하는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you're studying or preparing in order to get a job.

explain_en: This word appears a lot in the news and in official documents. In speech, '일자리를 찾고 있어요' or '취업 준비 중이에요' sounds much more natural. Its partner is '구인', looking for people to hire.

examples.en: His major is Korean linguistics.
I'm studying Korean linguistics at university.
In Korean linguistics, people study the sounds and grammar of the language.
My younger sibling is more interested in literature than in Korean linguistics.
Korean linguistics is hard too, but it's fun.
I got a book recommendation from a senior who majors in Korean linguistics.

explain: 한국 사람들이 '국어'라고 부르는 한국어를 연구하는 학문이에요. 말소리, 단어, 문법, 말의 역사를 다뤄요. 비슷한 말인 '국문학'은 글과 작품을 다루는 쪽이라 달라요.

phrases.en: My uncle is a famous scholar of Korean linguistics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국어학을 연구하는 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who studies Korean linguistics.

phrases.en: I'm taking a Korean linguistics class this semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 과목 이름처럼 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used like a course name at university.

phrases.en: I majored in Korean linguistics at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 중심으로 공부했는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what you focused on in your studies.

explain_en: It is the field that studies Korean, which Koreans call '국어'. It covers sounds, words, grammar and the history of the language. It differs from '국문학', which deals with Korean literature and texts.

examples.en: My father worked continuously at one company for thirty years.

examples.ko: 이 회사에서 10년 이상 근속하면 휴가를 더 줘요.
examples.en: If you stay at this company for over ten years, you get extra leave.

examples.ko: 오래 근속한 직원에게 상을 주기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to give an award to employees who have served a long time.

examples.ko: 그분은 한 병원에서만 근속하고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: He wanted to stay at just one hospital for his whole career.
I opened a shop with the severance pay I got after long service.
I received a gift for completing twenty years of service this year.

explain: 한 직장에서 계속 일할 때 쓰고, '근속 20년', '근속 연수'처럼 명사로도 많이 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '오래 다니다', '한 회사에 쭉 다니다'라고 해요. 보통 '20년 근속'처럼 기간과 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: If your years of service are long, your pay goes up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 직장에서 일한 해를 말해요. 회사 규칙이나 월급 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The number of years worked at one workplace. Common in talk about company rules and pay.

phrases.en: I received an award for ten years of service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기간 앞이나 뒤에 붙여 '그 기간 동안 계속 일했다'는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to a period to mean 'worked continuously for that long'.

phrases.en: I worked at one company for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '근속하다' 대신 이 말을 자주 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, people say this instead of 근속하다.
phrases.en_equiv: to stay at a job a long time

explain_en: It is used for continuing to work at one workplace, and the noun form appears in '근속 20년' and '근속 연수' (years of service). In daily talk people say '오래 다니다' or '한 회사에 쭉 다니다'. It usually comes with a length of time, like '20년 근속'.

examples.en: He is famous as a successful businessperson.
Business leaders gathered and talked about the economy.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 젊은 기업인이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a young entrepreneur someday.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 한 기업인이 학교에 큰돈을 기부했다고 해요.
examples.en: The news said a businessperson donated a large sum to a school.

examples.ko: 이 책은 유명한 기업인의 일생을 다뤄요.
examples.en: This book covers the life of a famous businessperson.
The government met with business leaders and heard their opinions.

explain: 기업인은 회사를 이끌거나 운영하는 사람을 폭넓게 말해요. '사업가'는 개인이 사업을 하는 사람, '경영자'는 회사를 관리하는 자리에 있는 사람이라서 느낌이 조금씩 달라요. 뉴스와 인터뷰에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: He is a young businessman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인이 사업을 하는 사람에 더 가까운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Closer to a person who runs their own business.

phrases.en: The head of that company is a woman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사를 관리하는 자리에 있는 사람에 초점을 둔 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the person in charge of managing a company.

phrases.en: I heard some new news at the business people's gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 기업인이 모이는 자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a gathering of several business people.

explain_en: 기업인 is a broad word for someone who runs or leads a company. 사업가 leans toward a person doing business on their own, and 경영자 toward someone in a management role, so the feel is a little different. You hear it often in news and interviews.

examples.en: I earned my degree through the self-study degree exams while working.

examples.ko: 독학사 시험을 준비하려고 인터넷 강의를 신청했어요.
examples.en: I signed up for online lectures to prepare for the self-study degree exam.

examples.ko: 독학사로 학위를 따는 게 어렵지 않대요?
examples.en: Is it true that getting a degree through the self-study system isn't hard?

examples.ko: 삼촌은 독학사 과정으로 심리학을 공부하고 있어요.
examples.en: My uncle is studying psychology through the self-study degree program.
My family was happy at the news that I passed the self-study degree exam.

examples.ko: 독학사 시험은 과목이 많아서 계획이 중요해요.
examples.en: The self-study degree exam has many subjects, so planning is important.

explain: 대학에 다니지 않고 시험에 합격해서 학사 학위를 받는 한국의 제도, 또는 그렇게 딴 학위를 가리켜요. 보통 '독학사 시험', '독학사 학위'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm going to take on the self-study degree exam next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험을 준비하겠다는 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say one will go after the exam.

phrases.en: I passed the self-study degree exam and got my bachelor's degree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the exam result.
phrases.en_equiv: to pass the self-study degree exam

phrases.en: In the self-study degree program, you take an exam for each subject.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학위를 따는 단계와 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the steps and method of earning the degree.

explain_en: It refers to the Korean system in which you earn a bachelor's degree by passing exams without attending university, or to the degree itself. It's usually said as '독학사 시험' or '독학사 학위'.

examples.en: My older brother works as a resident at the hospital.

examples.ko: 레지던트는 밤에도 당직을 서는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: Residents often take night duty too.
After graduating from medical school, I passed the residency exam.
The resident doctor examined the patient first.
He finished his pediatrics residency.

examples.ko: 드라마에는 잠도 못 자는 레지던트가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Sleepless residents often appear in dramas.

explain: 인턴을 마치고 한 과를 전문으로 배우는 수련 중인 의사를 말해요. 한국에서는 '인턴, 레지던트, 전문의' 순서로 올라가요. 환자에게는 보통 '선생님'이라고 부르고 '레지던트'는 병원 안 직급 이름이에요.

phrases.en: My friend works as a resident at a university hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to state this job.

phrases.en: I'm now a first-year resident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수련 몇 년째인지 말할 때 '1년차, 2년차'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 1년차, 2년차 to say which year of training it is.

phrases.example: 인턴과 레지던트는 모두 수련 중인 의사예요.
phrases.en: Interns and residents are both doctors in training.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 배우는 의사 단계를 말할 때 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together for the stages of doctors in training.

explain_en: A doctor in training who has finished an internship and is learning a specialty. In Korea the order is 인턴, 레지던트, 전문의. Patients simply say 선생님; 레지던트 is a rank used inside the hospital.

examples.ko: 이 상을 받게 되어 정말 명예로워요.
examples.en: I'm truly honored to receive this award.
He retired with honor.
Defending the country is an honorable job.
I think we lost with honor.
The players can't forget the honorable moment.
It's an honorable position, but it carries heavy responsibility.

explain: 사람들에게 존경받을 만하거나 자랑스러운 일·자리·행동에 써요. 평범한 기쁨에는 어울리지 않아요. 상을 받거나 큰 역할을 맡을 때 '영광이에요'와 같이 격식 있게 말해요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '명예로워요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Being chosen as the representative is an honor.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ 불규칙이라 '명예로운'으로 바뀌어 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a ㅂ-irregular adjective, it becomes '명예로운' to modify a noun.

phrases.en: A prize won by lying is not honorable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑스럽지 못하고 존경받기 어려운 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something not worth being proud of or respected for.

phrases.en: It is an honor to stand here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명예롭다'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 상을 받거나 큰 역할을 맡았을 때 격식 있게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning, used formally when receiving a prize or a big role.

explain_en: For jobs, positions or deeds that earn respect and pride; it doesn't suit ordinary happiness. When receiving an award or a big role it works like '영광이에요' in formal speech. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '명예로워요'.

p.n: Nearly identical; 명예스럽다 is the rarer variant.

examples.ko: 아버지는 목공을 배워서 책상을 직접 만드셨어요.
examples.en: My father learned woodworking and made the desk himself.
I attend a woodworking class every weekend.
Woodworking is my hobby, so I have many tools at home.
Simple woodworking needs a saw and a hammer.
The bookshelf made by woodworking looks sturdy.

examples.ko: 목공은 정확하게 재는 게 가장 중요하다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that measuring accurately is the most important thing in woodworking.

explain: 나무로 물건을 만드는 일을 가리키고, 그 일을 하는 사람은 보통 '목수'라고 불러요. 요즘은 가구나 소품을 직접 만드는 취미로도 많이 얘기해요.

phrases.en: I bought new woodworking tools.
phrases.nuance_ko: 톱, 망치처럼 나무 작업에 쓰는 도구를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to tools like saws and hammers used for woodwork.

phrases.en: I made a chair at a woodworking studio near my home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목공을 하거나 배우는 작업 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A workspace where people do or learn woodworking.

phrases.en: I do woodworking as a hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이 아니라 즐기는 활동으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is an enjoyed activity, not a job.
phrases.en_equiv: to do woodwork as a hobby

explain_en: It refers to the work of making things from wood, and the person who does it is usually called a '목수'. Today it is also talked about as a hobby of making furniture and small items yourself.

examples.en: My father is a carpenter who has worked for a long time.
A carpenter came and fixed the door.
A famous carpenter made this chair.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 목수가 되어서 집을 짓고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a carpenter and build houses later.
The carpenter is cutting wood.

examples.ko: 한옥을 짓는 목수는 특별한 기술이 필요해요.
examples.en: A carpenter who builds hanok needs special skills.

explain: 목수는 나무로 집이나 가구를 만드는 사람이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '목수님'이라고 해요. 한국어에서 나무를 다루는 일은 '목공'이라고도 하고, '목공 수업', '목공 체험'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 목수님, 이 문 좀 봐 주세요.
phrases.en: Mr. Carpenter, please take a look at this door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부를 때는 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 when addressing someone directly.

phrases.en: My father has worked as a carpenter for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업으로 목수가 하는 일을 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone does carpentry work as a job.

phrases.en: I want to become a carpenter someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or jobs.

explain_en: 목수 is a person who builds houses or furniture out of wood. When addressing one directly, people usually say 목수님. Working with wood is also called 목공, as in 목공 수업 or 목공 체험.

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 이 회사에 몸담았어요.
examples.en: I worked at this company for ten years.

examples.ko: 교육 분야에 몸담고 있는 분을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met someone who works in the field of education.

examples.ko: 옛날 자신이 몸담았던 부대를 보자 반가웠어요.
examples.en: He felt glad when he saw the unit he used to belong to.
Which club are you a member of?

examples.ko: 몸담은 지 오래된 곳이라 정이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I've been part of this place for a long time, so I've grown attached to it.

examples.ko: 그 일에 몸담으면서 많은 걸 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned a lot while working in that field.

explain: '회사에 몸담다', '이 분야에 몸담다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 단순히 '일하다'보다 그 조직이나 분야에 속해 오래 있었다는 느낌이 있고, 조금 격식 있게 들려요.

phrases.en: He has been in the medical field for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 그 분야에서 일하고 있다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the person is still working in that field.

phrases.en: The place where I used to work was a small company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금은 떠난 조직이나 회사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an organization or company you have left.

phrases.example: 삼 년째 이 회사에서 근무하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've been working at this company for three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸담다'보다 일반적이고, 직장에서 일한다는 사실만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral than 몸담다; it just states that you work at a workplace.

explain_en: It is used with '에', as in '회사에 몸담다' or '이 분야에 몸담다'. Compared with plain '일하다', it suggests belonging to that organization or field for a while, and it sounds a bit formal.

examples.ko: 무직자는 대출 심사가 더 까다로울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Loan screening can be stricter for people without a job.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 무직자지만 곧 취직할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm unemployed right now, but I'll get a job soon.

examples.ko: 무직자도 청년 지원금을 신청할 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard even people without jobs can apply for the youth support fund.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 무직자라서 카드를 만들기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: He had no job, so it was hard for him to get a card.
I gathered job information that unemployed people need.

examples.ko: 무직자 비율이 조금 줄었다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the share of people without jobs fell slightly.

explain: 서류나 통계에서 '직업: 무직'처럼 쓰는 딱딱한 말이라, 사람에게 직접 쓰면 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요. 일자리를 찾는 사람은 '구직자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I wrote 'unemployed' for my occupation on the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 통계에서 직업이 없는 상태를 적을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on forms or in statistics to state having no occupation.

phrases.en: I'm worried because I've been without a job for so long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 없는 기간이나 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a period or situation of having no job.

phrases.en: There is free training for job seekers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 찾는 사람을 말하며 '무직자'보다 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people looking for work and sounds gentler than '무직자'.

explain_en: It is a stiff word from forms and statistics, as in '직업: 무직', so using it directly about a person can sound cold. A person looking for work is called a '구직자' (job seeker).

examples.en: Einstein is a famous physicist.
My dream is to become a physicist.
Physicists discovered a new particle.

examples.ko: 그 물리학자는 우주에 대한 책을 썼어요.
examples.en: That physicist wrote a book about the universe.
My uncle is a physicist who works at a university.
The news interviewed a physicist.

explain: '과학자'가 넓은 이름이고, 물리학자·화학자·수학자는 분야별로 부르는 이름이에요. 대학 전공은 '물리학과'(또는 '물리 전공'), 연구하는 직업은 '물리학자'라고 구분해서 말해요. 소리, 빛, 힘, 에너지처럼 자연의 움직임을 다루는 사람에게 써요.

phrases.en: My older brother studies physics at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 대학의 전공을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the university major, not the person.

phrases.en: A physicist is one kind of scientist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학자는 넓은 이름이고 물리학자는 그 안의 한 분야예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 과학자 is the broad term and 물리학자 is one field within it.

phrases.en: Physicists study the universe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람을 말할 때 '-들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -들 when talking about several people.

explain_en: 과학자 is the broad word, and 물리학자, 화학자, and 수학자 name the specific fields. A university major is 물리학과 (or 물리 전공), while the working scientist is a 물리학자. It is used for people who study motion, light, force, and energy.

en: garbage man; sanitary worker; street cleaner

examples.en: Every dawn, the sanitation worker cleans the street.
I always feel grateful to the sanitation workers.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 미화원 선생님은 항상 웃으며 인사해 주세요.
examples.en: Our school's cleaning staff member always greets us with a smile.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에도 미화원들은 쉬지 않고 일해요.
examples.en: Even on rainy days, sanitation workers keep working without a break.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 분리해서 버리면 미화원이 일하기 편해요.
examples.en: If you sort your trash, it's easier for sanitation workers.

examples.ko: 아파트 미화원이 계단을 깨끗하게 닦아 주셨어요.
examples.en: The apartment cleaner wiped the stairs clean.

explain: 길이나 건물을 깨끗하게 하는 일을 하는 분을 정중하게 부르는 말이에요. 요즘은 '청소부'보다 '미화원'이 더 정중하게 들려요. 직접 부를 때는 '아저씨', '선생님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The sanitation workers start working early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분'을 붙여서 더 존중하는 느낌으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 분 makes it sound more respectful.

phrases.en: I greeted the sanitation worker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 이 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official name for this job.

phrases.en: The street cleaner is sweeping the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '미화원'이 더 정중하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 미화원 sounds more polite.

explain_en: It is a polite term for people who keep streets and buildings clean. These days '미화원' sounds more respectful than '청소부'. When addressing someone directly, people say '아저씨' or '선생님'.

en: to be knowledgeable; to be erudite

examples.ko: 우리 선생님은 역사에 대해 정말 박식하세요.
examples.en: Our teacher is really knowledgeable about history.

examples.ko: 박식한 사람과 이야기하면 배울 게 많아요.
examples.en: When you talk with a knowledgeable person, there is a lot to learn.

examples.ko: 그는 커피에 박식해서 추천을 잘해 줘요.
examples.en: He knows a lot about coffee, so he gives good recommendations.

examples.ko: 박식하다는 평을 듣지만 잘난 척하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is said to be well read, but he doesn't show off.
Grandfather is so knowledgeable that there is nothing he doesn't know.
You're so knowledgeable, so why do you say you don't know?

explain: 책이나 공부로 폭넓게 지식을 쌓은 사람에게 하는 칭찬이에요. 보통 '~에 박식하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 높일 때는 '박식하시다'예요. '해박하다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: Thanks to my knowledgeable friend, the homework was easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로, 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, used to praise a person.

phrases.en: My grandfather is very knowledgeable about Korean food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게 쓰는 높임 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form, used for elders or people you respect.

phrases.en: That person is well versed in the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박식하다'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 특정 분야를 깊이 아는 사람에게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to '박식하다', often used for someone who knows a field deeply.

explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who has built up wide knowledge through books or study. It is usually used as '~에 박식하다', and the honorific is '박식하시다'. '해박하다' is a similar word.

examples.en: The director picked a newcomer for the lead role.

examples.ko: 대표님이 저를 새 프로젝트에 발탁해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The CEO picked me for the new project.

examples.ko: 실력 있는 선수를 발탁하려고 전국을 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: They travel all over the country to pick talented players.
Everyone wonders what the criteria for picking are.

examples.ko: 처음으로 외국인 선수를 대표팀에 발탁할 거예요.
examples.en: For the first time, they will pick a foreign player for the national team.

examples.ko: 길에서 저를 가수로 발탁한 사람이 우리 삼촌이에요.
examples.en: The person who scouted me on the street as a singer is my uncle.

explain: '발탁하다'는 윗사람이나 조직이 숨은 능력을 보고 사람을 특별히 올려 쓸 때 써요. 뽑히는 쪽에서는 '발탁되다'라고 말해요. '뽑다'보다 좋은 기회를 준다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬하는 분위기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: A new actor was selected for the lead role.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발탁하다'의 피동 표현으로 뽑히는 쪽을 주어로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, with the person who is picked as the subject.

phrases.en: The director chose a newcomer for the lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이지만 특별한 기회를 준다는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday word, but it lacks the sense of giving a special chance.

phrases.en: The president picked me to be team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 나를 뽑아 준 것에 고마움을 담아 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful form expressing gratitude that a superior chose you.

explain_en: 발탁하다 is used when a superior or an organization spots hidden ability and gives the person a special role. From the chosen person's side you say 발탁되다. It feels warmer than 뽑다 because it implies a good opportunity, so it often appears in praising contexts.

dis.h: pick from many for a key role

p.n: 발탁하다 stresses singling someone out above others; 선발하다 suggests a selection process.

examples.en: I barely make a living with this job.

examples.ko: 아들이 이제 혼자 밥벌이할 나이가 됐어요.
examples.en: My son is now old enough to earn his own living.
It is hard to make a living from translation alone.
He made a living doing deliveries during the day.

examples.ko: 어떻게든 밥벌이해야 하니까 아무 일이나 해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: I have to earn a living somehow, so I have to try any job.
These days many people make a living from YouTube.

explain: '밥벌이를 하다'처럼 '를'을 넣어도 써요. '돈을 벌다'보다 먹고살기 위해 일한다는 절실한 느낌이 있어요. 구어에서 자주 쓰고, 격식 있는 글에서는 '생계를 유지하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I earn my own living now too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥벌이하다'를 띄어 쓴 모양으로 뜻은 같고, '제 밥벌이'처럼 꾸미는 말을 넣기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 밥벌이하다 with the same meaning; it makes it easy to add a modifier like 제 밥벌이.

phrases.example: 요즘 일이 없어서 밥벌이 걱정이 많아요.
phrases.en: I have no work lately, so I worry a lot about making a living.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹고살 일을 걱정할 때 '밥벌이'를 명사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 밥벌이 as a noun when worrying about making a living.

phrases.en: He makes a living with a small shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥벌이하다'보다 격식 있는 글이나 말에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal expression than 밥벌이하다, used in writing or formal speech.

explain_en: You can also say '밥벌이를 하다' with the particle '를'. Compared with '돈을 벌다', it carries a feeling of working just to get by. It is common in speech, and in formal writing people say '생계를 유지하다'.

examples.en: My dream is to be a translator who translates books.
The translator rendered the novel into Korean.
A famous translator translated this book.
I met a translator and heard their story.

examples.ko: 좋은 번역가가 되려면 두 언어를 잘 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To be a good translator you must know both languages well.
I gave a dictionary to my translator friend.

explain: '번역가'는 글을 번역하는 사람이고, 말로 바로 옮기는 사람은 '통역사'라고 해요. 책이나 영화 자막을 번역하는 사람은 번역가라고 해요. 직업을 말할 때는 '번역가예요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The film translator is making the subtitles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 분야를 붙여서 어떤 글을 번역하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a field before it to say what kind of text the person translates.

phrases.en: I want to become a translator later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: My older sister works as a translator at a publishing company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 직업을 말할 때 '-(으)로 일하다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-(으)로 일하다' to say what someone does for work now.

explain_en: 번역가 is a person who translates written text, while someone who interprets speech on the spot is a 통역사. People who translate books or film subtitles are called 번역가. When stating a job, you say 번역가예요.

examples.en: I met a patent attorney to file for a patent.
My uncle works as a patent attorney.
I heard the patent attorney exam is very difficult.
I left the trademark of the new product to a patent attorney.

examples.ko: 변리사가 되려면 어떤 공부를 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I need to study to become a patent attorney?
The patent attorney's office is on the third floor of this building.

explain: 특허나 상표 같은 지식재산 일을 도와주는 전문직이에요. 소송이나 일반 법률 문제는 '변호사'가 맡아요.

phrases.en: I met a patent attorney to register a trademark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특허나 상표 일로 상담할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when consulting about patents or trademarks.

phrases.en: The patent attorney's office is on the third floor of this building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 곳을 말할 때 뒤에 '사무실'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 사무실 after it to name the workplace.

phrases.en: My friend is preparing for the patent attorney exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 직업이 되기 위한 시험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the exam needed to become one.

explain_en: This is a professional who helps with intellectual property such as patents and trademarks. Lawsuits and general legal matters are handled by a '변호사' (lawyer).

examples.en: My father works as an office clerk at a small company.
I saw a notice saying they're hiring an office clerk.
The office clerk is organizing documents.
I asked the school office clerk for a certificate.
Attention to detail is important in office clerk work.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 병원에는 사무원이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: The clinic in my neighborhood has two office staff.

explain: 책상에서 서류, 접수, 회계 같은 일을 하는 사람을 직업으로 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '회사원', '직원', '사무직'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '사무원님' 대신 이름이나 직함을 써요.

phrases.en: I want to work in an office job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 사무 일의 종류를 말해요. 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the type of office work rather than the person. It is more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: My older brother is an employee at a small company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사무원보다 넓게 회사에서 일하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 사무원 for anyone who works at a company.

phrases.example: 우리 회사에서 사무원을 두 명 뽑아요.
phrases.en: Our company is hiring two office clerks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채용 이야기를 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about hiring.

explain_en: It names the job of someone who does desk work such as paperwork, reception or accounting. In daily speech, people more often say '회사원', '직원' or '사무직'. When addressing someone directly, use their name or title rather than '사무원님'.

en: person who helps bring something into being; (figurative) midwife

examples.en: He took on the role of founder of the new group.

examples.ko: 두 회사 합병의 산파역은 그 변호사였어요.
examples.en: The lawyer was the one who brought about the two companies' merger.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 산파역으로 나서서 문제가 풀렸어요.
examples.en: He stepped in as a go-between and the problem was solved.
Thanks to the person who got it started, our club was created.

examples.ko: 산파역이 없었다면 이 행사는 열리지 못했을 거예요.
examples.en: Without the person who set it in motion, this event could not have been held.

examples.ko: 두 사람을 소개해 주는 산파역을 했어요.
examples.en: I played the role of matchmaker by introducing the two.

explain: 아기를 받는 사람보다는 어떤 일이 생겨나도록 앞에서 도와준 사람을 비유할 때 많이 써요. '산파역을 맡다/하다'처럼 말하고 칭찬하는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 인터뷰에서 새로운 모임, 계약, 합의가 만들어진 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 선생님이 우리 동아리의 산파 역할을 했어요.
phrases.en: That teacher played the role of midwife for our club.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산파역'과 같은 뜻인데 '역할'을 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '산파역', with '역할' spelled out.
phrases.en_equiv: role as a midwife of something

phrases.example: 언니가 우리 가게를 여는 데 산파역을 맡았어요.
phrases.en: My older sister took on the role of midwife in opening our shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 생기도록 앞에서 이끌고 도와주는 역할을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes the lead in helping something come into being.
phrases.en_equiv: to take on the midwife role

phrases.example: 그 책이 새로운 제도의 산파역이 되었어요.
phrases.en: That book became the midwife of the new system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 책이나 사건이 시작의 계기가 되었을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for a book or event that triggered a beginning.

explain_en: It is more often used figuratively for a person who helped bring something into being than for someone who delivers babies. You say '산파역을 맡다/하다', and it carries a praising tone. It often appears in news and interviews about how a new group, contract or agreement came about.

examples.en: My father graduated from a commercial high school and worked at a bank.
At a commercial high school you learn accounting and management.
There are many seniors at the company who went to commercial high school.
I earned a certificate while attending a commercial high school.
I heard commercial high schools were popular in the past.

examples.ko: 상고 때 친구들과 아직도 자주 만나요.
examples.en: I still often meet my friends from commercial high school.

explain: '공고', '농고'처럼 학교 종류의 첫 글자를 따서 부르는 말이에요. 법원에서 쓰는 '상고'(윗법원에 다시 재판을 요청하는 일)는 소리만 같고 뜻이 전혀 달라요.

phrases.en: My younger brother attends a commercial high school and learns accounting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 학교의 학생이라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being a student at that kind of school.
phrases.en_equiv: to attend a commercial high school

phrases.example: 그분은 상고 출신이지만 큰 회사 사장이 됐어요.
phrases.en: He graduated from a commercial high school but became the head of a big company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 학교를 졸업했는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which school someone graduated from.

phrases.en: At a commercial high school, you learn business and management.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상고'의 원래 이름이고 조금 더 정확한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full name of 상고, a bit more formal and precise.

explain_en: Like 공고 and 농고, it takes the first syllable of the school type, here 상업고등학교. The 상고 used in courts, asking a higher court to review a case, only sounds the same and means something completely different.

examples.ko: 장마에도 시장 상인들은 생업을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: Even in the rainy season, market merchants kept up their livelihood.

examples.ko: 그는 생업을 잠시 접고 가족을 돌봤어요.
examples.en: He put his trade aside for a while and cared for his family.
Farming is the livelihood of the people in this village.

examples.ko: 생업에 바빠서 모임에 거의 못 나와요.
examples.en: I'm busy making a living, so I rarely come to meetings.

examples.ko: 큰 눈 때문에 생업에 지장이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The heavy snow disrupted people's livelihoods.

examples.ko: 저는 작은 가게를 생업으로 삼아 오래 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked for a long time with a small shop as my livelihood.

explain: '생업'은 먹고살기 위해 하는 일이에요. '직업'보다 '생계'에 무게가 있어서 '생업에 종사하다', '생업을 이어 가다'처럼 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. 취미나 부업은 생업이라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.en: The villagers make their living at sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 자주 쓰는 격식 있는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal collocation often seen in news and writing.
phrases.en_equiv: to be engaged in one's trade

phrases.en: He makes farming his livelihood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일로 먹고산다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say what someone earns a living by.

phrases.en: He supports his family's living on his own.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생업'이 일 자체라면 '생계'는 먹고사는 형편을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 'saengeop' is the work itself, 'saenggye' refers to making a living.

explain_en: 생업 is the work you do to make a living. It leans toward 생계 (the means of living) more than 직업 does, and it appears in news and writing as 생업에 종사하다 and 생업을 이어 가다. A hobby or side job is not called 생업.

dis.h: work one depends on to survive

p.n: 직업 is neutral; 생업 stresses that this is how he makes his living.
